subject: Post-call readout: private inference connectivity & performance — action plan
messages:
From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Tom Reed <tom.reed@acmeretail.com>, diego.fernandez@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call readout: private inference connectivity & performance — action plan

Tom / SRE team — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the action plan we discussed so there’s a single place to track next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

High-level ask from Acme: run Redwood Private in their VPC with predictable p95 latency and streaming start times for live checkout personalization. Key non-functional targets we aligned on during discovery:
- End-to-end p95 (app -> inference -> app): <= 200 ms for 128-token responses under normal traffic (non-peak).
- First-byte / stream-start latency (for streaming responses): <= 120 ms p95 (important for perceived latency on web checkouts).
- Sustained throughput target: 2,000 tokens/s (combined across instances) with bursts up to 5,000 tokens/s for 2–3 minute windows.
- Concurrent request target: 500 concurrent requests (avg payload ~64 tokens) with <5% throttling under SLO.

Network budgets we proposed to meet E2E SLOs (draft):
- App -> VPC egress / load balancer: <= 30 ms median; p95 <= 60 ms.
- VPC peering / private connectivity (Redwood Private -> Acme infra): allocation <= 30 ms p95.
- VPN / transit layer overhead (if applicable): plan for up to 20 ms additional overhead.
- Model compute + runtime (Redwood): target p95 compute <= 120 ms (depends on pinned model variant / quantization).

Immediate on-call action items (owners & ETA):
1) Network sanity & path baselining: Diego to run iperf3 + traceroute from Acme app subnet to the test endpoint, and capture p95/median for 1-minute and 5-minute windows. Deliverable: iperf results + packet path notes. ETA: 2027-04-27 EOD.
2) Peering & CIDR checklist: Tom to confirm the CIDR ranges for the peering and whether you will use AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering. Deliverable: confirmed approach + AWS account IDs. ETA: 2027-04-26.
3) Capacity profile & concurrency validation: Marissa to model instance sizing options for your traffic profile (requested 500 concurrency) and provide an expected cost/latency tradeoff table. Deliverable: capacity recommendation spreadsheet. ETA: 2027-04-29.
4) Streaming test plan: Vanessa to share a minimal streaming test harness (SSE + chunking) and expected payload shapes. Deliverable: private-deploy-test-plan.txt attached. ETA: 2027-04-26.

Attachments included: vpc-network-checklist.pdf (what we need from your network team), mutual-action-plan-ACME-7452.xlsx (milestones & responsibilities), private-deploy-test-plan.txt (streaming harness + test vectors).

Questions for Acme (please answer inline):
- Do you have a mandatory egress NAT/inspection appliance that will sit in the path? If yes, can we schedule a window to test its p95 behavior under sampling?
- Are TLS tunnels terminated inside your VPC, or do you expect Redwood to terminate TLS at a gateway we peer with?
- Do you have an existing websocket scale limit (we heard ~3k concurrently across services) we should plan around for streaming?

Next meeting: propose Wed 2027-04-28 08:00 PT for a short 30-min follow-up after Diego’s baseline tests.

Thanks — V.

--
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference — production-first LLM serving

(Attachment stubs: vpc-network-checklist.pdf, mutual-action-plan-ACME-7452.xlsx, private-deploy-test-plan.txt)

From: Tom Reed <tom.reed@acmeretail.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, diego.fernandez@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: SRE Team <sre@acmeretail.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call readout: private inference connectivity & performance — action plan

Vanessa — thanks for the crisp recap. A few clarifications from our side and a quick note on constraints: 

Clarifications / context:
- We can commit to the p95 end-to-end target of <= 200 ms as a business goal for the primary checkout flow, but our internal budget expects network transit to be <= 100 ms of that (so roughly app + network <= 100ms, leaving ~100ms for model/runtime).
- Our SREs confirmed we currently see median intra-region app->external-service latencies around 20-30ms; p95 for external services is often 60-90ms depending on destination.
- We will likely prefer VPC peering over PrivateLink for lower-latency traffic, but need to confirm from security about cross-account peering.
- TLS termination: we prefer to keep TLS termination inside our VPC for audit control — Redwood terminating inside a peered subnet should be fine if certs and audit logs are preserved.

Constraints / asks:
- We have a WAF/NAT appliance in the egress path for inspection during business hours. Can Redwood provide a recommended testing approach that simulates the appliance CPU backpressure?
- For streaming, we use long-lived websockets on the checkout page. Peak websocket concurrency is approximately 2,800 across services; streaming chunk sizes average 16–32 tokens.

We’ll take the CIDR list and account IDs offline to you (Tom) by tomorrow (2027-04-27). Diego, happy to coordinate on the iperf/traceroute windows — suggest we run 3x 2-minute runs at 9am/12pm/3pm PT to capture variance.

Tom
Tom Reed
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Retail
T: 978-555-0142

From: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, Tom Reed <tom.reed@acmeretail.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call readout: private inference connectivity & performance — action plan

Quick update after scheduling tests with Acme SREs:
- I scheduled the iperf3 + traceroute runs for 2027-04-27 at 09:00, 12:00, and 15:00 PT. Each run will be 120s, with both TCP and UDP tests and a 30s cooldown. I asked them to capture top-line metrics: median/p95 RTT, jitter, and throughput.
- I unpacked the draft network checklist and added a short checklist for packet capture windows (pcap) if we need to debug MTU/TCP MSS issues — note: MTU mismatches often explain unexpected 20–60 ms spikes on peered paths.
- For the streaming harness: I attached a minimal curl + SSE script to simulate chunked token delivery and measure first-byte latency. We’ll run it during the same windows.

Blockers / items I need:
- Tom: please confirm whether your inspection appliance performs deep packet inspection that terminates TLS (break & re-encrypt) or simply mirrors flow (NAT). That affects how we instrument the test.
- Marissa: can you start a quick instance sizing calc for the 500 concurrent request goal? If we assume 64 tokens/request and model p95 compute of 120 ms, I’ll validate network headroom required to keep E2E p95 <= 200 ms.

I’ll upload raw iperf results to the shared Drive link when complete and flag any path-level surprises.

- Diego

(Attachment stub: private-deploy-test-plan.txt, pcap-checklist.txt)
